summary.headline: Piramal Finance Q1 FY27 PAT rose 67% YoY to Rs 461 crore, with Growth AUM up 32% and Growth RoAUM at 1.9%.
summary.overview: Total AUM grew 25% YoY to Rs 1,06,940 crore, while Growth business AUM (retail plus wholesale, 98% of total) grew 32%. Growth business PBT was Rs 470 crore versus Rs 294 crore a year ago, and pre-provisioning operating profit rose 89% YoY to Rs 804 crore. Retail disbursements grew 44% YoY, and retail 90+ DPD stayed at 0.7%, though management flagged early-stage stress in IT-sector salaried borrowers and a small LAP uptick. The Board approved an enabling resolution to raise up to Rs 4,000 crore.

vs 6.9% in Q1 FY26 and FY26
Growth 1.6% vs 1.5% in Q4 FY26; legacy provisioning raised due to higher stage 2 PCR

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail AUM grew 32% YoY to Rs 91,249 crore; mortgages (HL plus LAP) grew 30% to Rs 61,199 crore, 67% of retail AUM. Unsecured (PL, UBL, digital, rural micro) grew 45% YoY to Rs 21,412 crore, 23% of retail AUM.

segments.name: Wholesale
segments.commentary: Wholesale AUM grew 27% YoY to Rs 13,238 crore, with a 70:30 real estate to CMML mix and average yield of 14.2%. Disbursed Rs 2,604 crore; repayments were Rs 1,932 crore (74% of disbursements).

segments.name: Legacy
segments.commentary: Legacy AUM fell Rs 355 crore to Rs 2,452 crore, now 2% of total AUM.

guidance_outlook: Reiterated original FY27 guidance on AUM growth, profit growth and RoAUM; Growth RoAUM expected to rise from 1.8-1.9% in Q1 to about 2.5% by Q4 FY27.
Retail OPEX to AUM (3.5% in Q1) expected to fall a further 40-50 bps over the next four to five quarters.
Gold loan branches to rise from 67 to 200 by end-March 2027; PL branch penetration targeted at 100% within two to three quarters.
Leverage target of 4.5-5x AUM to equity is under review; management expects higher leverage as the company moves to AA+.
Enabling resolution for up to Rs 4,000 crore of capital raise, timing and instrument open; no imminent acquisition.
capex_capacity: Branches: net 79 added in Q1 to 780 total; rural branches 178 (from 136); urban full-service branches reduced by eight to 535.
Gold loans network at 67 branches (phase two launched), targeting 200 by March 2027.
Regulatory CRAR 18.85%, with about Rs 9,000 crore gap between net worth and regulatory capital (about Rs 3,000 crore each from BAU deductions, DTAs and investment book); all Tier 1, no Tier 2.
Average quarterly capital consumption about 63 bps last year; DTA utilisation and investment sell-downs expected to release capital but not within the next two to three quarters.
demand_pricing: Retail disbursements grew 44% YoY in Q1 versus 34% in Q4 FY26 and 31% in FY26.
Wholesale: prepayments high; about 61% of FY27 contractual repayments already received; management attributes this mainly to operating cash flows running ahead of underwriting in real estate.

Mortgage competition: management says the number of players is unchanged; small-ticket housing (under Rs 35 lakh) industry growth is low single digit, and the company operates at about 12.5% yield in that segment.
Yield on loans stable at 13.2-13.4%; retail total income to loans down 26 bps YoY to 14.7% after fewer direct assignment (DA) sell-downs.
Partnerships/digital volumes rising with Fintech activity; more than 80% under FLDG; management will cut volumes if risk rises.

qa_highlights.question: Is salaried stress broader, given the strong salaried PL push? How is digital (embedded) scaling after an earlier slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Discomfort is limited to IT-sector salaried customers, mainly in South India; IT is about 13% of the unsecured salaried base. Early bounce rates are rising in secured products; unsecured is behaving well. Digital volumes are high because risk is at historically low levels and can be cut quickly.

qa_highlights.question: Will the elevated cost of funds be passed on to floating-rate mortgage customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds has not risen yet and was down; prime lending rate was not cut through the down cycle. Floating-rate customers will see rate moves in both directions, with lower amplitude.

qa_highlights.question: What drives RoAUM from 1.8-1.9% to 2.5% by Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 is the seasonal low because annual people-cost increments hit in Q1; a larger book originated through the year and flat staff cost should lift RoAUM by Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why are wholesale prepayments so high?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly operating cash flows ahead of underwriting in real estate; in CMML, refinancing by banks, capital-market raises and cash flows are all contributing.

qa_highlights.question: Why is disbursement yield above portfolio yield, and why has portfolio yield not risen?
qa_highlights.answer: Short-duration, higher-yield products are over-represented in disbursements, so AUM yield runs below disbursement yield structurally. Direction holds, but the gap will not close.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the capital raise needed when leverage is comfortable?
qa_highlights.answer: Regulatory CRAR of 18.85% (against 15% minimum and 18% comfort level) is well below what a net-worth-to-AUM view implies; the gap is about Rs 9,000 crore. The enabling resolution keeps Tier 2 and other instruments open.

qa_highlights.question: What is the early-bucket stress in IT-sector salaried loans, and is it flowing to later buckets?
qa_highlights.answer: Early bounce rates are up, not 90+ delinquencies; no flow to later buckets yet. Underwriting was tightened on the margin.

risks_watch: IT-sector salaried stress in South India, mainly secured products; early bounce rates rising, with flow to later buckets to be tracked.
LAP 90+ DPD small sequential uptick; four idiosyncratic cases cited; July trend to be watched.
Wholesale prepayments continue to reduce the book and growth.
Partnerships/digital volumes are cyclical and dependent on Fintech activity; the company says it will scale back if risk rises.
PCR rose on higher ECL assumptions and provision floors; management says PCR is not a target.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and the FY27 RoAUM path, but cautious on IT-sector salaried stress, which management repeatedly said is too early to call. Management was evasive on the NIM sequential move (attributed mainly to day count and fewer DA sell-downs) and on PCR, saying it is an output of model choices.
key_quotes: In Q1, we choose to reduce our DA sell-down and that mostly explained this slight moderation of NIM.
PCR is not a metric that one targets. PCR is an output, not an input to our decision-making.

growth.why: Management reiterated original FY27 guidance on AUM growth, profit growth and RoAUM, with Growth RoAUM targeted at about 2.5% by Q4 FY27 from 1.8-1.9% in Q1; backing is partial, citing retail disbursements up 44%, gold branches rising from 67 to 200 by March 2027, and opex-to-AUM falling 40-50 bps, but no quantified order book or capacity numbers tie to the guide.
